old: Antigravity access requires a paid Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, according to the developer announcement.[^1]
new: Individual Antigravity access requires a paid Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, according to the developer announcement and VentureBeat.[^1][^5]
why: VentureBeat specifies that the Pro or Ultra requirement applies to individual Antigravity access; business access comes through other plans.

support.quote: Individual Antigravity access requires Google AI Pro or Ultra.

old: Google lists flat pricing across Hydrogen's entire 1 million-token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, in its November 12 announcement.[^2]
new: Google's November 12 announcement gives standard API prices across Hydrogen's 1 million-token window of $1.50 per million uncached input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, including reasoning tokens.[^2][^5]
why: The launch post gives headline rates. Google’s pricing table and VentureBeat distinguish standard uncached input from discounted cached input and include reasoning in output.

support.quote: priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window
$1.50 per million uncached input tokens, $0.075 per million cached input tokens, and $7.50 per million output tokens, including reasoning tokens.

old: Google says that, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, the Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average.[^2][^5]
new: Google's launch post credits Orchestrator with near-Carbon success, 24% less quota and 19% faster completion on average on Terminal-Bench 4.0, while its Antigravity team gives the same figures for version 4.1.[^2][^5][^7]
why: Two Google launch publications give the same gains but identify different benchmark versions. Attribute each version to the team that reported it.
